summary: M4.3b LeaseManager, verification round. The four fixed minors are real in the staged bytes: the renewInterval comment now states a necessary-not-sufficient bound and hands the ratio to M1/M8; adopt() clears held/heldVersion on a lost CAS; a blank podId is refused in the constructor; and endpoint reaches Lease on BOTH the cold-start (new Lease(0, podId, endpoint, ...)) and takeover (current.takenOverBy(podId, endpoint, ...)) paths, each with its own test. A non-holder renew returns before any store call and the test asserts counts().total()==0, so the round-2 'non-holder destroys the fencing counter' mutation is dead. The two ttl assertions now match the full message 'ttl must be positive', which the renewInterval-vs-ttl message does not contain, so the positivity guard is individually pinned. The three round-1 test-review MAJORS are each now reachable and observed: StatBlindStore drives two contenders down the putIfAbsent path (a put would let both win and both new StatBlind tests fail), aHolderCanRenewRepeatedly renews five times so dropping heldVersion=won.get() fences the holder on renew two, and aNodeThatTookOverCanThenRenew fails if adopt records the version it CASed FROM. I read these rather than re-running the mutations (asked not to mutate the tree); the mutation measurements themselves are the test-reviewer's record. Request rates are unchanged and correct: acquire = stat + putIfAbsent (2) cold, stat + get + putIfMatch (3) on takeover, stat + get (2) when refused; renew = exactly one putIfMatch with no re-read (pinned by CountingBinStore delta == 1); release = one or zero. All O(1) per node per term, no LIST, nothing per record, shard, partition or index; rule 6 holds. No checkpoint pointer anywhere in LeaseManager, so M4.8 is not pre-empted. The file split is clean: StatBlindStore is a faithful pass-through over all ten BinStore methods plus close, blinding only stat, and src/test is the right home -- ingest/src/test/java/binjava/ingest/StoreFakes.java is the exact precedent (also split out at the 500-line limit, also a test-only decorator, also not in testFixtures), and no other module consumes it. Two cosmetic differences from that precedent, both below finding threshold: StatBlindStore is public where StoreFakes is package-private, and it inlines fully-qualified names where the precedent imports them. Suite MEASURED by me: ./gradlew test, 483 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped, sequencer 55 (26 pre-existing + 29 new) -- the backlog row's 472 -> 483 arithmetic checks out, as does 'three tests added and two ttl assertions tightened'. Carried minor 5 (the cost test names an acquire count it never asserts) is correctly carried, not fixed: the unasserted count is acquire-side, O(1) per node per term, so no mutation of it can produce a rate scaling with records, shards, partitions or indices, and theFirstAcquisitionUsesPutIfAbsent already pins puts()==1 there. Carried minor 1 (ambiguous renew) I verified as bounded exactly as claimed -- see finding 3 for the one part of its framing that is not accurate. Three new minors, none blocking.

findings.title: tryAcquire's unexpired-lease early return is the one branch that still leaves a stale belief in held
findings.failure_scenario: adopt() at line 202 now clears held/heldVersion on a lost CAS, with the comment 'Leaving a superseded lease in held would make held() report a term this instance does not hold'. The early return two lines above it does not, and that comment is therefore not true of the class. Concretely: podA acquires (held = epoch 0), podA GC-pauses past the TTL, podB takes over, podA calls tryAcquire rather than renew -- the call sequence the new test aLostAcquisitionDropsAnyBeliefFromAnEarlierTerm treats as supported, since it calls tryAcquire twice on one manager. stat is present, read() returns podB's unexpired lease, the method returns empty at line 140, and podA's held() still reports podA's epoch-0 term indefinitely. That is exactly the state minor 3's fix exists to prevent, reached by the sibling branch. Note the fix is not a blanket clear -- an instance may legitimately hold the unexpired lease it just read, and clearing there would make it forget a term it really holds -- so it has to be conditional on the read lease not being this instance's own (holderPodId plus epoch). Bounded in practice because the documented way to learn you are fenced is renew, which does clear, and no production caller exists yet; recorded rather than fixed.

findings.title: M4.12 is handed the `synchronized` pin on a justification this repo's own tests contradict, so the property will stay unpinned
findings.failure_scenario: The new M4.12 clause says 'a T1 test with a MemoryBinStore cannot make a JVM interleave deterministically' and that M4.12 'is the only place with the injectable interleaving that could kill the mutation'. Both halves are doubtful. (a) ingest/src/test/java/binjava/ingest/StoreFakes.java GatedCommit does precisely this today -- a store decorator holding putIfAbsent open on two CountDownLatches so DefaultIngestTest can observe a two-thread interleaving deterministically at T1 on a MemoryBinStore. The same shape (block one thread inside stat, run a second thread through the read-decide-CAS window, assert the invariant the monitor exists to protect) would kill the `synchronized` removal here. (b) M4.12's own row drives MANY LOGICAL PODS through the seam; logical pods each own their own LeaseManager, so no monitor is ever contended and removing `synchronized` from all four sites stays invisible in that harness too. The consequence is the failure mode the clause was written to avoid: the property is parked in a row that structurally cannot kill the mutation, the row asserts it is covered, and nobody looks again. Either the M4.12 clause states the mechanism it will actually use, or the property belongs in a row of its own naming the gated-decorator test.

findings.title: The ambiguous-renew minor is attributed to M4.10, whose row does not cover the lease
findings.failure_scenario: I verified the consequence claim and it is accurate: if the renew PUT lands but the response is lost, putIfMatch throws IOException, held/heldVersion keep the pre-PUT values, the node keeps sequencing while it does still genuinely hold the term (safe), its next renew CASes against the superseded version and loses, it stops, and nobody can take over until the landed lease expires -- a gap of at most TTL minus renewInterval, inside the TTL failover ADR-0007 already accepts. What is not accurate is the owner. M4.10's row is 'Commit idempotency on (podId, flushSeq) with lastAppliedFlushSeq per pod'; it is about commits and never touches the lease CAS, so nothing scheduled will address the lease case and the row reads as though something will. This is the same defect R4-2 describes -- a property assigned to a task that will not carry it -- and by the author's own non-negotiable-9 argument it is worth one sentence either saying plainly that this is accepted behaviour bounded by the TTL rather than debt, or giving it a row that names the recovery (re-stat on an ambiguous renew before concluding fenced).
